summary: Strengthen regulatory assessment, reliance, inspections, and digital workflow planning. Explore the course and build an institutional improvement roadmap.
lede: Medical product regulatory systems training helps authority staff, ministry officials, industry teams, and technical-assistance partners assess processes. Participants practise interpreting maturity evidence, mapping reliance pathways, coordinating dossier reviews or inspections, and designing digital submission workflows. They also create prioritised improvement plans and progress-reporting tools; detailed digital-system design and technical-standard implementation remain at overview level.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape or operate medicine and medical-device regulatory processes, from application review and inspection to institutional policy and technical assistance. Medicines registration assessors reviewing quality, safety, and efficacy submissions. Medical-device regulatory reviewers evaluating device dossiers and evidence. Good manufacturing practice inspectors planning and documenting facility inspections. Regulatory information-system officers managing application records and digital workflows. Regulatory reliance leads coordinating work-sharing and trusted-authority decisions. Health ministry pharmaceutical policy officials aligning regulation with system priorities. National regulatory authority quality managers monitoring process consistency and improvement actions. Pharmaceutical regulatory affairs specialists preparing Common Technical Document submissions. Medical-device quality managers aligning controls with ISO 13485 requirements. Technical-assistance advisers supporting regulatory capacity and workforce development.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with pharmaceutical or medical-device regulation, regulatory submissions, inspections, or health-product quality systems is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Participants can use an existing Excel-enabled laptop for workflow and action-tracking exercises; advanced digital-system concepts are introduced at overview level.
